Die Medizinische Hochschule Hannover (MHH), mit rund 10.000 Beschäftigten größter Landesbetrieb des Landes Niedersachsen, ist eine universitäre Einrichtung für Forschung und Lehre in der Human- und Zahnmedizin und ein Universitätsklinikum der Supramaximalversorgung. Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.About UsThe Hannover Medical School (MHH), with about 10,000 employees the biggest company of Lower Saxony, is a university institution for research and teaching in the human and dental medicine and a university hospital of supra-maximum medical care. Research, teaching, medical care and administration work hand in hand in the integration model at the MHH-campus.The Peter L. Reichertz Institute for Medical Informatics (PLRI) is one of the largest university centres for medical informatics in Germany. It belongs to two leading universities, is situated in one of Europe's most research-intensive regions, and offers excellent opportunities for research. In interdisciplinary projects, the PLRI collaborates with health centres, research institutes, corporations, and public institutions in order to shape the future of the health system and medicine. The activities range from diverse topics on the local level, to regional, national, and global collaborations.The research group "Clinical Data Science" focuses on the detection of novel routine clinical and -omics biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis to personalize and thus improve patient treatment. To achieve this, we integrate phenotypical information and routine clinical as well as (multi)-omics data by high-dimensional statistics and state-of-the-art artificial intelligence to gain novel insights into underlying disease pathomechanisms. Moreover, we are interested in developing and implementing research data platforms for complex (multi-)omics data. The project "MALDIDive: Enabling AI Research with Public MALDI-TOF Fingerprints across Microbial Diversity", to be carried out within an interdisciplinary research team and funded by the German Research Foundation, will establish a well curated data platform of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry datasets from the Leibniz Institute German Collection of Mircoorganisms and Cell Cultures GmbH (DSMZ). We are looking for an enthusiastic PostDoc who is interested in omics data platform development and deployment for future AI use.Your Responsibilities- data platform architecture, backend, and frontend development as well as deployment for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry database/platform and associated metadata- development of interactive data visualization concepts and their implementation into data platform- development and realization of short explanatory videos for platform users- co-organization and co-leading of stakeholder workshops to define user requirements and conduct user test cycles- presentation to the scientific community, i.e., by publishing in high-level journals and via presentations at international conferences- close collaboration with interdisciplinary project partners from AI / data science, analytical, and micro­biological research communities, particularly the DSMZ- bachelor / master student co-supervisionYour Profile- PhD / Dr. rer. nat. / Dr.-Ing. degree in data science / bioinformatics / computational biology / informatics / physics or similar research fields- expertise in the work on databases, interactive platform development, -omics and languages: VueJS, TypeScript, SQL, PYTHON, R Shiny, nginx, Docker, etc.- proficiency in English (written and oral)- desired: experience with code documentary systems and RestAPI- desired: knowledge of jobs.occupation: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project (Fachinformatiker/in - Anwendungsentwicklung)
jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow . The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.Your tasks- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.Your profile- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Hanieh Saeediat hanieh.saeedi@senckenberg.de

The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedElectronics Engineer (m/f/d)Your positionAs an Electronics Engineer, you will support cutting-edge experimental physics research by developing reliable, high-performance electronic systems in close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff.- Develop, design and implement analogue and digital electronic systems for experimental physics applications.- Translate scientific and technical requirements into robust electronic concepts, circuits and complete devices.- Design, assemble, commission and test printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic instruments, from initial concept through prototyping to deployment in the laboratory.- Diagnose, troubleshoot and optimise existing electronic systems and measurement equipment.- Develop firmware for microcontrollers and support the integration of hardware, firmware and software components.- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.Your background and skills- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.Our offer- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.- Opportunities for professional development and further training.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the applicable public-sector collective agreement, depending on qualifications and professional experience.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticketYour applicationThe Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all background.The Max-Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals.To apply please complete the online application form and attach you English CV and motivation letter as well as all relevant certificates latest 15th November, 2026.If you have any questions, please feel free to contact contact Dr. Friedjof Tellkamp by email at friedjof.tellkamp@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:friedjof.tellkamp@mpsd.mpg.de) or Dr. Lars Tiemann at lars.tiemann@mpsd.mpg.de (lars.tiemann@mpsd.mpg.de) .Detailed information about the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter and the online application portal can be found on our website at: https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs (https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs)We look forward to your application.
